_note: The entertainment allowance deduction for an employee paid by the Government, TY 2025-26 only, outside the new regime (D-105; rulebook SAL-ENTMT-001). Income-tax Act, 1961 s.16(ii) (thc.nic.in p.140): "a deduction in respect of any allowance in the nature of an entertainment allowance specifically granted by an employer to the assessee who is in receipt of a salary from the Government, a sum equal to one-fifth of his salary (exclusive of any allowance, benefit or other perquisite) or five thousand rupees, whichever is less" — two limits, not capped at the allowance received (the words do not say so). Not in the new regime: s.115BAC(2)(i) as substituted by Finance Act, 2023 s.52 lists "clause (ii) or clause (iii) of section 16" (p.34). TY 2026-27: the Income-tax Act, 2025 has no counterpart — s.19(1) Table Sl. 1–14 has no such entry and a full-text search of the gazette finds no "entertainment allowance" (rulebook SAL-ENTMT-001) — so the rule has no TY 2026-27 version and the allowance is ordinary salary. In every regime as a row; the new regime forbids it through DIS-NEW-TAX-REGIME-NO-EXEMPTION, whose basis REG-NEW-TAX-REGIME-NO-EXEMPTION (S2 s.202(2)(a); 1961 s.115BAC(2)(i)) every explanation cites (D-166).
